narrative:
The model estimated a 45.0% chance that you would be a bad credit risk. That is not a certainty, but it was high enough under the bank’s lending cutoff that your application was denied; it means applicants with a similar profile are expected to have meaningful repayment difficulty.

The strongest influence on the decision was the amount of credit you requested. At 2,712 DM, it was below the approved-applicant average of about 3,020 DM, so this factor actually worked in your favor and reduced your risk. The second most important factor was your checking account status. Because it was below zero DM—an overdrawn or negative position—and only about 12.6% of approved applicants had this status, it pushed the prediction toward bad credit and was the main reason for denial. The third factor, your installment rate, was 2% of disposable income versus an approved average near 3%, so this also helped you.

To improve a future application, focus on bringing your checking account into positive balance and keeping it there, avoiding overdrafts or missed payments, and reducing existing debt obligations. You may also ask the bank about a guarantor or co-applicant and consider reapplying after several months of stable account balances and repayment history.
